Install libretro-vice-xvic on Omarchy

This is the VIC-20 core of VICE (the Versatile Commodore Emulator) built for the libretro/RetroArch framework. It emulates Commodore's 1980-era VIC-20 home computer so its games and programs can run inside RetroArch on a modern Linux machine. As a libretro core it has no standalone window or menu of its own; RetroArch provides the surrounding interface.

  1. Open a terminal.
  2. Run the install command:
    omarchy pkg add libretro-vice-xvic-git
  3. Check it landed. Pacman should list version r21255.fdda9d0-1:
    pacman -Qi libretro-vice-xvic-git

Open and use libretro-vice-xvic

libretro-vice-xvic has no window of its own: it is a command-line tool, library or system component. To see the commands it added to your PATH:

pacman -Ql libretro-vice-xvic-git | grep /usr/bin/

libretro-vice-xvic requirements and compatibility

  • RetroArch installed to load and run the core
  • VIC-20 software/ROM images supplied by the user

Dependencies Omarchy installs for you

  • glibc
  • libretro-core-info
  • libgcc_s.so
  • libstdc++.so

Pricing and license

Free and open source. License: GPL-2.0-or-later.

Uninstall libretro-vice-xvic

omarchy pkg drop libretro-vice-xvic-git

Frequently asked questions

How do I install libretro-vice-xvic on Omarchy?

Open a terminal and run omarchy pkg add libretro-vice-xvic-git. The download is 896.2 KB and it takes 2.3 MB once installed. Omarchy pulls in any dependencies automatically.

Is libretro-vice-xvic free?

Free and open source. The package is licensed GPL-2.0-or-later.

How do I uninstall libretro-vice-xvic?

Run omarchy pkg drop libretro-vice-xvic-git. It removes the package from your system.

What does libretro-vice-xvic depend on?

The package declares 4 dependencies: glibc, libretro-core-info, libgcc_s.so, libstdc++.so. Omarchy installs them for you.

Is libretro-vice-xvic a desktop app?

No. libretro-vice-xvic has no window of its own; it is a command-line tool, library or system component.

Is libretro-vice-xvic in the official Omarchy repo?

Yes. It is published as libretro-vice-xvic-git (version r21255.fdda9d0-1) in the official Omarchy package repository. Libretro makes it. Project site: https://github.com/libretro/vice-libretro.
